28fefe16db.what_happened: California has issued an investigative subpoena to AI chip designer Nvidia following the departure of its longtime CEO Jensen Huang. Attorney General Rob Bonta is investigating whether Nvidia or Huang helped China obtain advanced chips or secret information, potentially misleading investors and the public.
details: California's top law enforcement official, Rob Bonta, announced on Thursday that the state is examining if corporate securities laws were violated by misleading the public and investors. The inquiry centers on Nvidia, which is based in Santa Clara, California, amidst what Bonta called a messy transnational situation regarding advanced tech transfers to China.

The investigation follows revelations earlier this month that former CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang had an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy and executive at Singapore data center firm Megaspeed. Megaspeed is a major Nvidia customer, and US lawmakers have asked the Department of Commerce to probe if it diverted chips to China, though Megaspeed claims such allegations lack verifiable proof.

Huang admitted to extramarital affairs and stepped down last week following claims of relationships with subordinates. Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones stated the company will not reinstate Huang, even though Huang stated he would be honored to return and tech figures like Elon Musk supported him, while company shares have plunged 22% since the affair was reported in early November.
28fefe16db.why_it_matters: The probe examines whether Nvidia violated state corporate securities laws by misleading investors and the public regarding confidential information or advanced chips reaching China.
key_facts: California served an investigative subpoena on AI chipmaker Nvidia.
Attorney General Rob Bonta is probing if China got advanced chips or confidential data.
Longtime CEO Jensen Huang recently stepped down amid reports of workplace affairs.

Alice Huang worked at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a major Nvidia customer.

Board chair Harvey Jones said Nvidia will not reinstate Huang, despite Elon Musk's backing.
28fefe16db.blurb: California has subpoenaed Nvidia to investigate whether China improperly accessed advanced chips following former CEO Jensen Huang's scandal.
28fefe16db.spoken: California officials are turning up the heat on Nvidia. Attorney General Rob Bonta has issued an investigative subpoena to the Santa Clara-based chip designer. Regulators want to know if actions by the company or its former longtime chief executive Jensen Huang allowed China to obtain advanced chips or confidential data, which could violate state securities laws against misleading investors. This comes right after Huang stepped down over extramarital relationships with subordinates, as well as an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based customer Megaspeed who is suspected of being a Chinese spy. Some US lawmakers want federal authorities to see if Megaspeed diverted chips to China, though the company denies unsupported claims. Despite support from tech leaders like Elon Musk, Nvidia's board says Huang will not be reinstated, especially after the company's shares dropped 22 percent.

details: Police arrested a 33-year-old suspect in Katunayake. The arrest was made during a raid by officers of the Negombo Divisional Crime Investigation Bureau in the early hours of Thursday (19), after a tip-off.

fb3e06a92d.what_happened: A 36-year-old man who was being held by police in Matale died after he became ill. Officers took him to the Matale District General Hospital, and he was pronounced dead at around 12.45 a.m. The police said he had been arrested for allegedly having ICE drugs.
details: The source is a Newswire report. A 36-year-old man was arrested for allegedly having ICE narcotics. He died after suddenly becoming ill while held at the Matale Police Station early today (20).

The police said he was rushed to the Matale District General Hospital after he fell ill in the detention cell. He was pronounced dead at around 12.45 a.m. The man was identified as a resident of Dilenagama, Ampitiya, Kandy.

He was arrested last morning (19) in the Hithgolla area of Matale by the Matale Police Anti-Corruption Unit. He was accused of having 3,010 milligrams of ICE, and he reportedly became ill around 11.00 pm after being detained. The police said he was heavily addicted to drugs and had several drug cases pending at about 10 police stations, including Kandy and Grandpass; a Post mortem is scheduled for today and Matale Police are investigating the death.

18ccc76ffe.what_happened: The Court of Appeal emphasised that elephants must be safeguarded as a vital national resource and heritage. The bench made this observation while hearing a legal challenge against a government policy permitting firearms for farmers. The court noted that international tourists visit Sri Lanka to see wildlife rather than large buildings.
details: The Sri Lanka Wildlife and Nature Protection Society filed a petition asking the court to overturn the government's decision to issue guns to farmers for crop protection. The case was heard on Tuesday by Court of Appeal President Justice Rohitha Abeysuriya and Justice Priyantha Fernando. The petitioner's lawyer, President's Counsel Sanjeewa Jayawardena, warned that giving firearms to farmers seriously imperils wild animals, especially elephants, noting that the tusker Kawanthissa had already been shot dead.

Jayawardena informed the judges that the minimum landholding required to obtain a firearm had recently been reduced by the government from five acres to two acres, which could lead to many more weapons being handed out. He revealed that 305 firearms were distributed by 2002, 490 by 2026, and data indicated a total of 3,207 firearms have been issued so far.

Justice Abeysuriya stated that the court places significant weight on protecting the environment and wildlife, stressing that elephants are a national asset and that tourists do not travel to the island for tall buildings. The court said it would seek proposals from all parties on ways to keep elephants safe. Named respondents include Deputy Defence Minister retired Major General Aruna Jayasekara, Defence Ministry Secretary Air Vice Marshal Sampath Thuyacontha, and Environment Minister Dr. Dammika Patabendi.
18ccc76ffe.why_it_matters: The case highlights concerns that loosening rules on issuing firearms to farmers puts endangered wildlife, particularly the national elephant population, at severe risk.
key_facts: The Court of Appeal considered a petition against issuing firearms to farmers to guard crops.
Court President Justice Rohitha Abeysuriya said foreign tourists visit for nature, not large buildings.
The land eligibility threshold for getting a firearm was lowered from five acres to two acres.
Lawyer Sanjeewa Jayawardena noted that 3,207 firearms have reportedly been issued so far.

The petitioner highlighted the fatal shooting of the tusker Kawanthissa.
Court adjourned the matter until November 30 to seek safety proposals.
18ccc76ffe.whats_next: The Court of Appeal will obtain submissions from all parties on measures to safeguard elephants and will continue hearing the petition on November 30.
18ccc76ffe.blurb: Sri Lanka's Court of Appeal has called for elephant protection, saying tourists visit for wildlife, not large buildings.
18ccc76ffe.spoken: Sri Lanka's Court of Appeal has stepped in to stress the vital importance of protecting the nation's wild elephants. While hearing a legal challenge against a government decision to hand out firearms to farmers, Court President Justice Rohitha Abeysuriya remarked that foreign tourists come to Sri Lanka to experience its natural heritage, not to look at large buildings. The court heard that authorities lowered the land size needed to get a gun from five acres down to two, and over three thousand firearms have already been distributed. With animals like the tusker Kawanthissa recently shot dead, wildlife advocates want the policy scrapped. The judges will collect safety ideas from all sides and resume hearings on November 30.
18ccc76ffe.subject: Elephant protection

6a7f3a3a3d.what_happened: Parliament passed the second reading of the 2027 Budget by a 97-vote majority following a seven-day debate. The vote concluded with 157 votes in favour and 60 votes against. This is the 81st Budget in the history of Sri Lanka.
details: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake presented the proposal on November 12 in his role as Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development. Debate began on November 13 and finished at 6.30 pm on November 20, marking the third budget presented by the National People’s Power government. Records show 157 MPs voted in favour, 60 MPs voted against, and no MPs abstained.

The 2027 Budget estimates total government spending at Rs. 7.933 trillion, up from Rs. 7.309 trillion in revised 2026 estimates. Total revenue is projected at Rs. 6.15 trillion, while revenue and grants reach Rs. 6.18 trillion. These figures leave an estimated budget deficit of Rs. 1.753 trillion, representing 4.5% of Gross Domestic Product.

Alongside these proceedings, Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe announced headline inflation will likely exceed 9% this month. In judicial matters, Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama ordered a progress report on the Krrish inquiry by December 01, while MP Chamara Sampath Dassanayake was further remanded until November 27.
key_facts: The 2027 Budget second reading passed with 157 votes in favour and 60 against.
A 97-vote majority cleared the proposal after a seven-day parliamentary debate.
President Anura Kumara Dissanayake presented the proposal on November 12.
Government expenditure is estimated at Rs. 7.933 trillion for 2027.

6a7f3a3a3d.whats_next: The Committee Stage debate begins on November 21 and runs across 19 days until December 14, meeting at 9.30 am each day except Sundays and public holidays, ahead of a final vote at 6.00 pm on December 14.
6a7f3a3a3d.blurb: Sri Lanka's Parliament has approved the second reading of the 2027 Budget by a 97-vote majority.
6a7f3a3a3d.spoken: Sri Lanka's Parliament has approved the second reading of the 2027 Budget by a ninety-seven-vote majority. After seven days of debate, one hundred and fifty-seven lawmakers voted in favour, while sixty voted against, with no abstentions. Presented by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake as Finance Minister, this is the eighty-first budget in the country's history. It outlines government spending of seven point nine three three trillion rupees and projects an estimated deficit of one point seven five three trillion rupees. Meanwhile, Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe warned that inflation will likely top nine percent this month. Lawmakers now move to the Committee Stage debate, which continues until the final vote on December 14.
6a7f3a3a3d.subject: 2027 Budget

96a7f9767d.what_happened: A Missouri state court judge has approved a $7.25bn settlement by German firm Bayer to resolve lawsuits alleging its Roundup weedkiller causes cancer. The deal addresses around 65,000 claims from people who fell ill after using the product. The ruling potentially closes out litigation that has troubled the company for nearly a decade.
details: Judge Timothy Boyer of a St Louis court ruled that the $7.25bn agreement was fair, reasonable, and adequate. He rejected complaints that individual payments were too small compared to earlier settlements, warning that further delays would force cancer victims, including those who are terminally ill, to wait indefinitely for financial relief.

Originally announced in February, the settlement aims to conclude almost all existing and future Roundup cases across the country. Bayer had been confronted with roughly 65,000 lawsuits in US state and federal courts from users who alleged they developed cancer from domestic or workplace exposure.

Bayer bought Monsanto, the manufacturer of Roundup, for $63bn in 2018, which led to widespread legal battles and caused its share value to slide by 46%. Although Bayer paid $10.9bn to resolve large portions of the litigation in 2020, a previous $1.25bn plan covering future claims failed to secure court backing.

Bayer maintains that Roundup and glyphosate do not cause cancer and are supported by decades of scientific research. Five months prior to this approval, the US supreme court issued a 7-2 ruling overturning a $1.25m award to Missouri resident John Durnell, ruling that federal pesticide rules override state-level failure-to-warn claims. About 200 cases continue in federal court, outside of this agreement.
96a7f9767d.why_it_matters: The approval provides financial relief to tens of thousands of cancer patients while removing a massive legal risk that has depressed Bayer's stock by 46% since 2018.
key_facts: Judge Timothy Boyer approved Bayer's $7.25bn Roundup settlement in St Louis, Missouri.
The agreement addresses about 65,000 lawsuits linking the weedkiller to cancer.
Bayer bought Monsanto for $63bn in 2018, after which its share price fell 46%.

Plaintiffs' lawyer Christopher Seeger noted the supreme court decision limited victims' court options.

96a7f9767d.whats_next: Lawyers aim to distribute the settlement funds to Roundup victims as quickly as possible, while Bayer continues to defend roughly 200 pending federal lawsuits.
96a7f9767d.blurb: A Missouri judge has approved Bayer's $7.25bn settlement over claims that its Roundup weedkiller causes cancer.
96a7f9767d.spoken: A major legal battle in the United States has reached a critical turning point. A state judge in St Louis, Missouri, has officially approved Bayer's seven point two five billion dollar settlement over its Roundup weedkiller. The German company has faced around sixty-five thousand claims from people who say using the product at home or at work gave them cancer. Judge Timothy Boyer dismissed objections about payout amounts, noting that delaying approval would force victims, including those with terminal cancer, to wait years for compensation. Bayer has seen its stock drop forty-six percent since buying Monsanto for sixty-three billion dollars in 2018. The company insists the product is safe, and lawyers now plan to distribute the funds as swiftly as possible.
96a7f9767d.subject: Roundup cancer litigation

933288238d.what_happened: Denmark expelled Russia's defence attaché after accusing Moscow of plotting to kill Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner at a concert near Copenhagen. Police arrested three men with firearms and knives five minutes before the scheduled performance, which was cancelled. Two Danish men were charged with attempted murder and assisting a foreign intelligence service.
details: Denmark summoned the Russian ambassador and announced the expulsion of Russia's defence attaché within seven days, with Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen stating that they have exposed Russia. He also said Denmark is considering suspending Schengen visas for Russians and is working with the EU to tighten visa rules.

PET assessed that Russian intelligence planned to kill US-Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner, whose real name is Albert Viktorovich Vasiliev, during a concert on 25 September in a Copenhagen suburb. Police stopped three men in a car near the venue north of Copenhagen with two loaded pistols and two knives at about 9.55pm, five minutes before the concert; one had bought a ticket, and the concert was cancelled, while a fourth suspect was arrested later. The suspects are linked to the banned gang Loyal to Familia, and two Danish men were charged under Section 108 with assisting a foreign intelligence service and attempted murder, denying wrongdoing.

PET head Rasmus Kieffer-Kristensen said the assassination attempt is not something previously seen in Denmark and shows Russia is increasingly aggressive and risk‑taking, adding that Russian intelligence attempted to carry out an execution in Denmark. Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen stated that Denmark faces a cornered Russia and must not waver in supporting Ukraine. European Council President Antonio Costa called the alleged attempt unacceptable and promised the EU's full backing against Russian hybrid attacks.

Russia's Foreign Ministry Maria Zakharova said Moscow will give an appropriate response, while the Russian embassy called the expulsion vengeful and claimed no evidence of Russia's involvement. Copenhagen has previously accused Russia of hybrid attacks, including a drone shutdown of Copenhagen airport in September 2025. PET also said in September that Russia was recruiting Danish citizens to help plan sabotage against Danish defence firms with ties to Ukraine, and Russia has denied involvement in such operations.
933288238d.why_it_matters: The alleged plot illustrates the threat Russia poses to Denmark and the EU, prompting diplomatic expulsions and visa restrictions.

FM Lars Løkke Rasmussen announced the decision and visa suspension plans.

933288238d.whats_next: Russia promised an appropriate response; Denmark is considering suspending Schengen visas for Russians and working with the EU to tighten visa rules.
933288238d.blurb: Denmark expels Russian defence attaché over alleged plot to kill Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner at Copenhagen concert.
933288238d.spoken: Good morning, listeners. In a significant diplomatic development, Denmark has expelled Russia's defence attaché after accusing Moscow of plotting to kill the Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner at a concert near Copenhagen. The rapper, who holds both Ukrainian and U.S. citizenship, was scheduled to perform on September 25th, but police arrested three men with firearms and knives just before the show, leading to its cancellation. Danish intelligence says the plot was linked to a banned gang and Russian intelligence services. Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen announced the expulsion and said Denmark is considering suspending Schengen visas for Russians, while working with the EU to tighten visa rules. The European Union has pledged full support, calling the alleged attempt unacceptable. Russia has threatened an appropriate response, but Denmark's prime minister insists on continuing support for Ukraine. This incident highlights the growing tensions and the importance of standing firm.
933288238d.subject: Russia-Ukraine conflict

1785b21d52.what_happened: Four people died in four separate road accidents across Sri Lanka on Friday (20), police said. The dead included a 79-year-old woman from Ratmalana and a 23-year-old motorcyclist from Malwatta 02. The crashes were reported in Malabe, Mount Lavinia, Eravur and Sammanthurai.
details: Police said four people were killed in four different road accidents on Friday (20), in Malabe, Mount Lavinia, Eravur and Sammanthurai. The victims included a 79-year-old woman and a 23-year-old motorcyclist.

In Mount Lavinia, a 79-year-old woman from Ratmalana was hit by a car while she was crossing the Galle–Colombo Road. She was badly injured and taken to Kalubowila Hospital, where she died later. Police arrested the car driver.

On the Batticaloa–Trincomalee Road, a 42-year-old motorcyclist from Manampitiya died in a crash involving several vehicles. Police said a lorry heading towards Valaichchenai hit two motorcycles travelling in front of it, then crashed into a car near the Kattupalli Road junction. Both motorcyclists were badly hurt and taken to Eravur Hospital, where one of them died, and the lorry driver was arrested.

On the Kalmunai–Ampara Road, a 23-year-old motorcyclist from Malwatta 02 died after hitting a lorry coming from the opposite direction; the motorcyclist and the pillion rider were taken to Ampara Hospital with serious injuries, and the rider later died of his injuries. Separately, a pedestrian was struck by a motorcycle running along Wanaguru Mawatha from Horahena Junction towards Hokandara Junction; both were badly hurt and taken to Mulleriyawa Hospital, where the pedestrian died, and police said the pedestrian has not yet been identified. The police stations concerned are still investigating all four accidents.

The car and lorry drivers were arrested, the pedestrian is unidentified, and investigations continue.

1785b21d52.spoken: Police in Sri Lanka are reporting a deadly day on the roads. Four people lost their lives in four separate accidents on Friday the twentieth. The crashes were reported from Malabe, Mount Lavinia, Eravur and Sammanthurai. In Mount Lavinia, a seventy-nine year old woman from Ratmalana was crossing the Galle to Colombo Road when a car struck her. She died at Kalubowila Hospital, and the driver was arrested. On the Batticaloa to Trincomalee Road, a lorry heading towards Valaichchenai ran into two motorcycles and then a car near the Kattupalli Road junction. A forty-two year old rider from Manampitiya died at Eravur Hospital, and the lorry driver was arrested. A twenty-three year old from Malwatta zero two died at Ampara Hospital after hitting an oncoming lorry. And a pedestrian, still unidentified, died at Mulleriyawa Hospital after a motorcycle struck them. Police are investigating all four.

d9d55b2a7c.what_happened: President Donald Trump held a White House press conference on Friday as a test for possible 2028 successors. He asked JD Vance and Marco Rubio to stay still for 90 minutes while he rambled about potholes. Stephen Miller attracted attention as Trump’s favourite offspring.
details: President Donald Trump held a White House press conference on Friday as a test for possible 2028 successors. He asked JD Vance and Marco Rubio to stay still for 90 minutes while he rambled about potholes. The room was crowded, the air‑conditioning hissed, and a sound engineer adjusted the microphone, giving Trump an echo.

Trump referenced his trilateral meeting with China and Russia, likening it to the Yalta conference and noting that the United States, Russia and China control 92% of the world’s nuclear arsenal. He also mentioned his uncle John Trump, an MIT electrical engineer, and claimed a genetic blessing from that background. Rubio then defended the president’s outreach to those leaders, arguing that their combined nuclear power makes regular dialogue essential and dangerous to ignore.

A reporter asked which of the two would make a better president after Trump, and Trump swatted the question away without answering. Vance replied that he would support the president’s Iran policy even though he opposes the war, while Rubio smiled knowingly. The event was described as the first audition for the 2028 election and the article expects further careful positioning in the coming campaign.
d9d55b2a7c.why_it_matters: It is the first audition for the 2028 presidential election.
key_facts: President Donald Trump held a White House press conference on Friday as a 2028 succession audition.
He challenged JD Vance and Marco Rubio to stay still for 90 minutes without reacting.
Stephen Miller sat beside them and attracted attention as Trump’s favourite offspring.
Trump said the United States, Russia and China hold 92% of global nuclear power.
Rubio defended Trump’s engagement with those nuclear powers, calling the idea of avoiding dialogue absurd and dangerous.
Vance pledged to back the president on Iran, and the event is the first 2028 audition.
d9d55b2a7c.whats_next: More needle‑threading is expected in the upcoming campaign.
d9d55b2a7c.blurb: Trump turned a White House press conference into a 2028 succession audition, testing Vance and Rubio while Stephen Miller stole the spotlight.
d9d55b2a7c.spoken: On Friday the president held a White House press conference that was billed as the first audition for the 2028 election. Donald Trump stood at the podium and challenged his potential heirs, JD Vance and Marco Rubio, to stay composed for ninety minutes while he rambled about potholes and other topics. Stephen Miller, his favourite child, sat nearby and drew attention. 81135dd7ec.what_happened: A Dutch court issued a preliminary injunction on November 20. It blocked BYD from selling its Fang Cheng Bao Ti7 SUV in the European Union. The court found the Ti7 had a similar overall visual impression to the Land Rover Defender and that this infringed design rights.
details: The source is a newswire. BYD, a Chinese electric vehicle giant, got a legal setback. A Dutch court in The Hague issued a preliminary injunction on November 20 after a design rights dispute with British luxury vehicle maker Jaguar Land Rover (JLR).

The court found the BYD Ti7 created a similar overall visual impression to the Land Rover Defender. It cited similarities in overall proportions, rounded shoulders, wheel arches, and window lines. The injunction stopped BYD from importing, manufacturing, offering for sale, selling, storing, or delivering the Ti7 in the European Union.

The restriction applied only to the Ti7 and did not affect BYD’s other vehicles. The Fang Cheng Bao Ti7 is a seven-seat plug-in hybrid SUV from BYD’s Fang Cheng Bao sub-brand. BYD maintained the vehicle was independently designed and did not infringe JLR’s intellectual property rights.

The decision was a legal victory for JLR, which sought to protect the Defender SUV design. But the ruling was a preliminary injunction, not a final judgment after a full trial. The court noted BYD had no concrete plans to bring the Ti7 into the European market at that time, and the case highlights increasing competition as Chinese brands expand.
81135dd7ec.why_it_matters: The case highlights increasing competition between Chinese automakers and established European manufacturers as Chinese brands continue expanding their international presence.

a4db39a80c.what_happened: Russia launched a major overnight attack on Ukraine, firing ballistic missiles at bridges in Kyiv and railway stations across the country. The strikes hit key crossings in the capital and left at least nine people dead. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called it one of the most massive strikes of the war so far.
details: Russia launched a major overnight attack across Ukraine, targeting bridges in Kyiv and railway stations with ballistic missiles. Key crossings in the capital were hit during the nationwide assault. At least nine people were killed.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky described the strike as one of the most massive of the war so far. The attack came days after Ukraine badly damaged the strategically important Crimean Bridge. Russian President Vladimir Putin had threatened to retaliate for that earlier attack on the bridge.

The Kremlin built the Crimean Bridge to link Russia and the occupied peninsula. The latest strikes took place during a flurry of talks about the war. They also came as the Kremlin pushed back against a US claim that Russia could be open to Western-backed security guarantees for Ukraine.
BBC reporter Sarah Rainsford was in Kyiv after the night of strikes to report on what happened.

48f549e40a.what_happened: Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores, a Mexican drug lord on the FBI's 10 most wanted list, was arrested after a shoot-out with Mexican authorities. Special forces detained him and seven others in Guasave, Sinaloa on Friday, and the US is now seeking his extradition. Seven suspects and four Mexican army members were killed.
details: Mexican authorities have arrested Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores, a drug lord on the FBI's 10 most wanted list, after a shoot-out. Mexico's defence secretariat said special forces detained him and seven other people in Guasave, in the state of Sinaloa, on Friday. Seven suspects were killed in the operation, and so were four members of the Mexican army who were travelling to reinforce security in Guasave.

The secretariat said the forces used US intelligence on his whereabouts, moved in with what it called "stealth and surprise" and set a perimeter to stop him escaping and reinforcements arriving, but came under attack from gunfire and explosives before entering the property and arresting him. Videos circulating online appear to show helicopters firing streams of bullets towards the ground in Guasave, and people at a baseball stadium fleeing as they hear shooting sounds. Eight people were arrested in total, including his second-in-command, who is also his cousin, and his brother-in-law, the group's financial operator; a grenade launcher, other weapons, drugs and cash were seized, and while Meza Flores, his cousin and his brother-in-law were flown to Mexico City to face prosecution, the other five remained in Sinaloa.

Meza Flores, who is 44, leads the Meza Flores Organisation, also known as the Guasave Cartel, and is thought to have been active in drug trafficking since the 1990s, evading authorities until now by keeping a relatively low profile. He was wanted in Mexico on organised crime charges, and was first charged with drug trafficking in the US in 2012 and charged again in 2019, accused of conspiring to manufacture and distribute large quantities of cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine and marijuana between 2005 and 2019. He was originally a high-ranking member of the Beltrán Leyva Organization, but a split between rival factions led to a surge of violence and prompted him to set up his own cartel by 2013, and his group has since fought what US officials called an "extremely violent turf war" with the Sinaloa Cartel, one of the most powerful trafficking gangs, which operates in the same region.

The FBI accuses him of "flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin and other deadly drugs", and the US is seeking his extradition. He was added to the bureau's most-wanted list in 2025, accused of "heinous crimes" including kidnapping, extortion and torture, after Mexican authorities reportedly linked his cartel to 20 million fentanyl pills seized in 2024; then-acting FBI director Brian Driscoll said Meza Flores and his organisation had unleashed a "scourge of illicit drugs" into the US via its southern border with Mexico. Mexico has stepped up efforts to tackle drug-related crime after coming under pressure from US President Donald Trump, who made stemming the flow of drugs across the southern border a key election pledge, while Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has taken a tougher stance on cartels to resist US intervention on Mexican soil, welcoming closer collaboration but resisting US boots on the ground. The US Consulate General in the city of Hermosillo said it was "monitoring reports of ongoing security operations, armed clashes, road blockades, and vehicle fires that occurred overnight in Ahome, Guamúchil, Guasave, and Navolato" after the arrest, and advised US citizens to stay alert for potential violence and residents to remain sheltered in place.
48f549e40a.why_it_matters: Mexico has stepped up its fight against drug-related crime after pressure from US President Donald Trump, and the arrest removes a man the FBI accuses of flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine and heroin; the US is now seeking his extradition.

4795cded67.what_happened: Minister Nalinda Jayatissa told Parliament that former President Ranil Wickremesinghe spent Rs. 1,010 million on 33 foreign trips during his 26 months in office. By comparison, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake spent Rs. 31.7 million on eight foreign trips over a similar period.
details: Minister Nalinda Jayatissa shared the figures in Parliament on Saturday, November 21. He said former President Ranil Wickremesinghe spent Rs. 1,010 million on 33 foreign trips during his 26 months in office.

According to the minister, 421 people went with Wickremesinghe on those 33 trips. The trips stretched from his visit to the United Kingdom on September 17, 2022, to his visit to India on June 8, 2024.

President Anura Kumara Dissanayake made eight foreign trips in his first 26 months, costing Rs. 31.7 million in total. The minister added that the current President did not claim any extra or combined allowances for those visits.

That's a lot of globe-trotting, and four hundred and twenty-one people went along with him. So the numbers show a big gap between the two leaders' travel spending, and it's now on the public record in Parliament.

dd194f367f.what_happened: Qatari mediators visited Tehran for two hours of talks with Iranian officials on Friday night, as Iran's foreign minister demanded the US meet conditions to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's president called the situation a 'silent economic war,' while the IRGC commander inspected an underground missile facility. The US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, triggering regional conflict and disrupting global oil shipping.
details: A Qatari delegation traveled to Tehran on Friday night and held two hours of discussions with Iranian officials, Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said. He stated that Iran is in contact with mediators both in person and virtually to see if diplomacy can be given another opportunity. Gharibabadi added that the talks have not yet become formal negotiations, but if they do, technical details of Iran's nuclear programme would be discussed, though Iran insists its enriched uranium must not leave the country.

Gharibabadi also said Iran views the US economic blockade as an act of war and will take any action necessary to break it. US President Donald Trump told Fox News he wants a permanent deal preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon, calling Iranian officials 'very, very difficult' and accusing them of breaking deals. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the ongoing talks must be given a chance and the blockade lifted rationally, but stressed that discussion on the Strait of Hormuz is pointless unless Iran's demands are met.

Iran's conditions include ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions, and ending the US counter-blockade of Iranian ports. Araghchi said reopening the strait is not difficult and only requires the US to accept reasonable conditions in accordance with international law. He added there is no solution unless Washington acknowledges its mistakes and fulfills previous commitments. Iran has restricted shipping through the strait, which normally carries about a fifth of the world's oil, since the war began, and the US has imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports in response.

President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran is facing a 'silent economic war' tougher than a missile war, blaming a group of bullies, oppressors, and coercers for trying to bring down the country, but noted Iranian businesses have managed market conditions well and the government is working to avoid winter power cuts. Meanwhile, IRGC commander Major-General Ahmad Vahidi toured an underground missile facility with Brigadier General Majid Mousavi, head of the IRGC Aerospace Force, and was briefed on readiness and missile programme developments. The visit follows the Aerospace Force's unveiling of a new underground facility earlier this month displaying ballistic and cruise missiles and launchers.
dd194f367f.why_it_matters: The conflict has disrupted shipping, pushed up global energy prices, and drawn in countries across the region, affecting global oil supply and regional stability.

dd194f367f.spoken: Qatari mediators have arrived in Tehran for talks with Iranian officials, as the country pushes the United States to accept its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The delegation met for two hours on Friday night, and Iran's deputy foreign minister says they're exploring whether diplomacy can get another chance. But Tehran is holding firm: its enriched uranium stays in the country, and it wants the US to end the war on all fronts, unfreeze Iranian assets, lift oil sanctions, and stop the naval blockade on Iranian ports. President Masoud Pezeshkian calls it a silent economic war tougher than any missile attack, while the Revolutionary Guard commander just toured an underground missile facility. The US and Israel struck Iran on February 28, triggering a wider conflict that's disrupted shipping and driven up global oil prices. President Trump says he wants a permanent deal to stop Iran getting a nuclear weapon, but calls Iranian officials very difficult. For now, the talks are not yet formal negotiations, and Iran says discussing the strait is pointless until its demands are met.
